title: The Revival, knowledge
hookLine: the Revival opens with the book of knowledge: knowledge that leads to action
tomorrow: you finished the prayer. were you actually there for any of it?
last: A LIGHT CAST IN THE CHEST.

cards: The saved posts folder. The podcast at double speed. The book about habits you finished and then changed no habits.
It's easy to know far more than we do. You know exactly what's right, and you still haven't done it.
Al-Ghazali seems to have known that feeling well, because after his crisis he wrote a huge work, the Revival of the Religious Sciences, and he opened it with a book on knowledge.

teach.b: Not knowledge as trivia. His concern is knowledge that turns into action, and he warns against learning that only decorates the learner.
He leans on a prayer of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Sahih Muslim, asking refuge from knowledge that does not benefit. The Qur'an asks believers why they say what they do not do.
Knowledge, in the Revival, isn't finished until it moves your hands.
Now, a week of it, held up together. A thin crescent, greeted like a guest: a new month, in peace. Rain asked for, and asked to move, because the point was benefit: beneficial rain.
A hospital doorway, and a sick man allowed to argue back: a purification. A sneeze, answered in three turns: mercy on you. A scholar who called his questions a gift: thirsty for truth.
And the doubt that no proof could end: a light cast in the chest. Notice the thread.

teach.h: SMALL, AND ALL OF IT DONE.
teach.b: Each of these is small, and none of them is only an idea.
Every one of them is something a person says or does on an ordinary day. That's al-Ghazali's whole case in one week.

how: Al-Ghazali's Revival of the Religious Sciences is read and taught in Muslim study circles book by book, beginning with the Book of Knowledge; Muslims also pray the Prophet's words seeking refuge from knowledge that does not benefit.

o: al-Ghazali's great work, opening with the book of knowledge
a yearly festival when mosques are freshly painted
the reawakening of the dead on the last day

games.q: the week's lines — tap the pairs.

s: the Revival opens with a book on prayer
it opens with the Book of Knowledge.
the Prophet asked refuge from knowledge that does not benefit
a prayer kept in Sahih Muslim.
for al-Ghazali, the more you know, the better, whatever you do with it
he warns against learning that only decorates the learner; knowledge is for action.

games.q: you've watched hours of videos on being kinder to your little brother. he just knocked on your door asking for help with homework. what fits al-Ghazali's first book?
o: watch one more video first so you do it right.
open the door; this is where the knowing gets finished.
tell him you're busy; the learning was the important part.
games.why: knowledge in the Revival isn't finished until it moves your hands. the knock is the test.

practice: Name one small thing you already know you should do: a reply you owe, a dish, a glass of water for someone. If it fits inside the sit, do it now, slowly. If not, write its first step and leave the pen on top of the page.
